correctness.rationale: For every ordered rung set, exhaustive graph-theoretic cycle deletion yields exactly the product of twice the consecutive column gaps, with independent uniform rail-cut choices. Coefficient extraction gives \(a_{n,k}=2^{k-1}\binom{n+k-1}{2k-1}\). The factorial majorant proves convergence of the critical partition and all rung-count masses in total variation. Riemann sums establish the Dirichlet spatial density; conditioning makes the rail-cut marks independent and uniform. The finite path-Laplacian transfer-current kernel has Neumann cosine eigenvalues and a summable spectral bound, giving trace-norm convergence to the stated DPP. For subcritical and supercritical couplings its spectral sum and fixed eigenvalues prove the count dichotomy. The standalone checker independently passed 627 finite and numerical assertions; asymptotic validity is supplied analytically, not inferred from tests.

originality.rationale: Prior exact finite ladder transfer-current kernels, infinite-ladder renewal formulas and classical determinantal existence theory were identified and credited. None of the materially inspected texts states the combined critical \(n^{-2}\) continuum Neumann DPP, odd-conditioned Poisson count, open-boundary Dirichlet position law, and independently marked rail-cut limit. The wheel critical law is mathematically distinct: even-conditioned Poisson count with cyclic Dirichlet(2) gaps. The new theorem includes a separate all-size proof. A general unlocated continuum theorem remains a residual priority risk; absence in searched records is not itself proof of uniqueness. Archive suitability is supported by the 1994 original infinite-ladder study (year only) and a directly relevant 2016 probability text; these were not misused to assert text-wide absence of a stronger theorem.
residual_risks: A broader continuum limit theorem for vanishing conductances on strips or Neumann resolvent determinantal processes could imply the unmarked marginal without using the displayed parameters.

value.rationale: There is a motivated scale where two nearly disconnected rails require one bridge but have an \(O(1)\) surplus of additional bridges. The exact classification of the full rare-rung spatial and marked-cut law, including sharp quadratic scale, odd Poisson count and boundary-sensitive Dirichlet gaps, supplies nontrivial natural probability invariants and a finite-interval continuum limit. Its open-boundary parity distinction from the cyclic wheel model is structurally meaningful, rather than cosmetic parameter substitution.
